headline: City to acquire 98 Maverick Street building for $1 through right of first refusal.
summary: The city sold the building in 1983 for $1 and kept a right to buy it back for $1. A one-year lease pays $4,171 a month, with the tenant covering utilities and insurance, and Savita Health now runs early intervention services there. A phase one environmental report found no current recognized environmental conditions, though earlier asbestos and lead work was noted. The lot behind the building, 0 Maverick Street, is listed as park property and would need a separate review before any sale.
decisions: Approved accepting the order to acquire 98 Maverick Street for $1 by unanimous consent.
discussion: 98 Maverick Street purchase: Members discussed the one-year lease at $4,171 a month and whether the city should buy the building now or wait for the lease to end. Support was voiced for buying it, and one view was that some rent could be set aside to pay for an appraisal and legal costs before any future sale.

Parkland behind the building: Members disagreed on whether the lot at 0 Maverick Street needs Parks Board review and state approval before any sale. A public speaker said she was concerned about the park and the future of the building.

Possible housing use: A view was raised that the old schoolhouse could suit homes, and whether a development program tied to Water Street could apply. The community development director said that program focuses more on business and economic development.
